subject: general
question: Which of the following exponents does NOT play the Sitar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pt Shiv Kumar Sharma.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma**

 
 
• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian classical musician and **santoor player.**
 
• He is credited with adapting the santoor for Indian classical music.
 
• He collaborated with Indian flutist Hariprasad Chaurasia under the collaborative name Shiv–Hari.
 
• He composed music for many Indian films including Faasle (1985), Chandni (1989), and Lamhe (1991).
 
• He was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award **in** 1986, the Padma Shri **in** 1991, and the Padma Bhushan **in** 2001.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ustad Vilayat Khan**

 
 
• Ustad Vilayat Khan was an Indian classical sitar player. 
 
• He is credited with the creation and development of gayaki ang (an attempt to mimic the sound of the human voice) on the sitar.
 
• He recorded his first 78-RPM disc at the age of 6, and gave his last concert in 2004 at the age of 75.
 
 
 
• **Anoushka Shankar**
 
 
• ​Anoushka Shankar is a** British-Indian-American sitar player**.
 
• She was the youngest and first woman to receive a British House of Commons Shield.
 
• She has had **7 Grammy Awards nominations **and was the first Indian musician to perform live and to serve as a presenter at the ceremony.
 
• She performs across multiple genres and styles - classical and contemporary, acoustic and electronic.
 
 
 
• **Pt Ravi Shankar**
 
 
• **Pt ​**Ravi Shankar was an **Indian sitarist** and composer.
 
• He became the world's best-known export of North Indian classical music in the second half of the 20th century.
 
• He influenced many musicians in India and throughout the world.
 
• He was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999.
